one_sentence_pitch.question: One-sentence pitch
one_sentence_pitch.answer: Slotwise helps small appointment-based studios (demo: Isar Wellness, a wellness studio offering massages, facials and reflexology) take online bookings from a clear itemized price menu so that no-shows drop and cancelled slots get refilled automatically from a waitlist.

the_problem_being_solved.question: The problem being solved
the_problem_being_solved.answer: Small service businesses such as massage and wellness studios, physiotherapists, tutors and repair shops take most bookings by phone, WhatsApp or a paper diary. The owner answers calls during treatments, prices are only explained verbally, and customers regularly forget appointments or cancel at the last minute. A cancelled 60-minute massage at EUR 70 usually stays empty because there is no quick way to tell the customers who wanted that time. Big platforms (Fresha, Treatwell) exist, but they take commission or feel too heavy for a one- to three-person studio. Today owners cope with phone reminders by hand, WhatsApp broadcasts and simply accepting the lost income.

type_of_app.question: Type of app
type_of_app.answer: Booking or scheduling (e.g., salon, clinic, class slots)

how_you_will_know_it_is_working.question: How you will know it is working
how_you_will_know_it_is_working.answer: Within 3 months: no-show rate below 5% (from roughly 10-15% today), at least 50% of cancelled slots refilled through the waitlist, and at least 60% of bookings made online instead of by phone. The owner dashboard shows all three numbers.

front_end_most_important_user_journey_st.question: Front end: Most important user journey, step by step
front_end_most_important_user_journey_st.answer: Customer taps the studio's booking link on Instagram or Google Maps -> sees the itemized menu on Home -> taps Book next to 'Deep tissue massage 60 min, EUR 70' -> adds the add-on 'Hot stones, +15 min, EUR 12' -> picks therapist Lena -> picks Friday -> taps the free time 17:00 -> enters name, email and phone -> checks the summary (massage EUR 70 + hot stones EUR 12 = EUR 82, 75 minutes, pay at the studio) -> taps Confirm booking -> sees the confirmation screen and receives an email with the itemized summary and a manage link -> 24 hours before, gets a reminder email and taps 'Confirm I'm coming'. If she has to cancel instead, the slot is automatically offered to the first matching person on the waitlist.

front_end_navigation_map_in_words.question: Front end: Navigation map in words
front_end_navigation_map_in_words.answer: Customer: Home -> Book -> Booking confirmation -> (email link) Manage booking. If no times are free on Book, the customer joins the waitlist and stays on Book with a success message. Waitlist email link -> Claim waitlist slot -> Booking confirmation (or 'No thanks' -> Home). Owner: Home footer 'Studio login' -> Owner login -> Dashboard; the side menu reaches Bookings, Services & add-ons, Therapists & hours and Waitlist. Log out returns to Home. Any owner screen opened without a valid session goes to Owner login. If saving fails, stay on the same screen and show the error next to the field or at the top.

back_end_extra_endpoints_not_tied_to_a_c.section: Back End — Actions, Rules and API
back_end_extra_endpoints_not_tied_to_a_c.question: Back end: Extra endpoints not tied to a control
back_end_extra_endpoints_not_tied_to_a_c.answer: GET /public/studio (studio name, address, phone, hours and policy for the Home header). GET /auth/me (check the owner session on page load). POST /internal/run-jobs (protected by a secret header; sends due reminders, expires waitlist offers and passes them to the next person; called every 15 minutes by a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow, because the free host sleeps and cannot run its own scheduler). GET /health (returns status and app version; used by the CI/CD smoke test after every deploy).

back_end_actions_the_app_must_perform.section: Back End — Actions, Rules and API
back_end_actions_the_app_must_perform.question: Back end: Actions the app must perform
back_end_actions_the_app_must_perform.answer: Calculate free start times from working hours, days off, existing bookings, total duration and buffer. Check the chosen time is still free at the moment of saving (inside one database transaction). Save the booking together with its itemized lines, copying the current name, duration and price of every service and add-on. Create or reuse the customer by email. Email an itemized confirmation with the manage link. Send a reminder email 24 hours before with one-click confirm and cancel links. On cancellation, free the slot and offer it to the first matching waitlist entry by email with a 30-minute claim link; if it expires or is declined, offer it to the next one. Turn a claimed offer into a booking with source 'waitlist'. Let the owner mark bookings done or no-show, adjust the final items, and email a final itemized receipt with a receipt number. Count no-shows and late cancellations per customer. Calculate the dashboard numbers. Export bookings to CSV.

back_end_business_rules_and_calculations.section: Back End — Actions, Rules and API
back_end_business_rules_and_calculations.question: Back end: Business rules and calculations
back_end_business_rules_and_calculations.answer: A therapist can never have two overlapping bookings; the buffer after each service counts as blocked time. Bookings need at least 2 hours' notice and can be made at most 60 days ahead. Start times are on 15-minute steps and must fit completely inside the therapist's working hours. Total duration = sum of service minutes + add-on minutes; blocked time = total duration + the largest buffer of the chosen services. Total price = sum of (unit_price_snapshot x quantity) of all booking items. Prices are copied into each booking item at booking time, so later menu price changes never change existing bookings or receipts. Inactive services and add-ons are hidden from customers but stay on old bookings. Cancellation is free up to 24 hours before; later cancellations are allowed but flagged as late_cancellation. A booking can only be marked done or no-show after its start time, and only done bookings can get a receipt. Waitlist offers go to entries in join order whose date, time window, therapist preference and total duration fit the freed slot; only one open offer per slot at a time; an offer expires after 30 minutes. Customers with 2 or more no-shows are highlighted for the owner (no automatic blocking in version 1). All money is in EUR with 2 decimals; all times are in Europe/Berlin.

back_end_error_situations_and_messages.section: Back End — Actions, Rules and API
back_end_error_situations_and_messages.question: Back end: Error situations and messages
back_end_error_situations_and_messages.answer: Time already booked -> 400 'That time was just taken. Please pick another.' Booking less than 2 hours ahead or more than 60 days ahead -> 422 'Please choose a time between 2 hours and 60 days from now.' Missing or invalid email or phone -> 422 'Please enter a valid email address' / 'Please enter your phone number.' Unknown booking or offer link -> 404 'Booking not found. Please check the link in your email.' Expired waitlist offer -> 410 'Sorry, this offer has expired.' Cancelling an already cancelled or finished booking -> 400 'This booking is already cancelled or finished.' Already on the waitlist for that day -> 409 'You are already on the waitlist for this day.' Wrong login -> 401 'Email or password is wrong.' Owner page without session -> 401, the front end redirects to Owner login. Duplicate service name -> 409 'A service with this name already exists.' Unexpected error -> 500 'Something went wrong. Please try again.'

back_end_user_types_and_what_each_can_do.section: Back End — Actions, Rules and API
back_end_user_types_and_what_each_can_do.question: Back end: User types and what each can do
back_end_user_types_and_what_each_can_do.answer: Customer (no account): view the menu, book, join the waitlist, and through the secret email link view, confirm or cancel only that one booking and see its receipt. Customers can never see other customers' data. Owner (email and password): everything in the owner area, including services and prices, therapists, hours, days off, all bookings, statuses, final items, receipts, waitlist, dashboard and CSV export. Therapists don't log in in version 1; the owner manages their schedules.

database_how_the_tables_connect_in_words.question: Database: How the tables connect, in words
database_how_the_tables_connect_in_words.answer: One customer can have many bookings and many waitlist entries. Each booking belongs to exactly one customer and one therapist and has one or more booking items. Each booking item is a snapshot of one service, one add-on, or an extra line added on the day. One service can have many add-ons; each add-on belongs to one service. Therapists and services are many-to-many through TherapistServices. Each therapist has many working-hour rows and days off; a day off without a therapist closes the whole studio. A waitlist entry can point to the booking it turned into. Studio and Owners each hold a single row in version 1.

scope_must_have_features_for_version_1_m.question: Scope: Must-have features for version 1 (maximum 3)
scope_must_have_features_for_version_1_m.answer: 1) Customers book online from the itemized service menu (services + add-ons, therapist, free time) and see an itemized price summary before confirming. 2) Automatic emails: itemized confirmation, 24-hour reminder with one-click confirm/cancel, and automatic waitlist offers when a slot is cancelled. 3) Owner area: calendar/list of bookings, mark done or no-show, adjust final items, send the itemized receipt, and a dashboard with no-show rate and waitlist-refilled slots.

scope_nice_to_have_features_for_later.question: Scope: Nice-to-have features for later
scope_nice_to_have_features_for_later.answer: Deposits or no-show fees through Stripe for new customers. SMS or WhatsApp reminders. Therapist logins to see their own schedule. Google Calendar sync. Gift vouchers and packages (e.g., 5 massages). Reviews after a visit. Multiple languages (German and English). Several studios on one platform. Group classes with a capacity.

scope_what_the_app_should_not_do.question: Scope: What the app should NOT do
scope_what_the_app_should_not_do.answer: No online payments in version 1. No customer accounts or passwords (the email link is enough). No storage of health or medical information. No multiple studios or branches. No group classes. No therapist logins. No AI features yet.

build_similar_apps_for_inspiration.answer: Fresha, Treatwell and Calendly. Slotwise is simpler and built for one small studio, with no commission. build_anything_else_the_ai_should_know.question: Build: Anything else the AI should know
build_anything_else_the_ai_should_know.answer: MAIN PURPOSE: this app exists to practise CI/CD with GitHub Actions and deploying to a free cloud tier, so it must stay lightweight. Hosting: ONE free Render web service runs FastAPI, which also serves the plain HTML/CSS/JS front end as static files (no separate front-end deploy, no Node build step). Database: SQLAlchemy with DATABASE_URL; SQLite locally and in tests, Neon free PostgreSQL in production; create tables with a simple startup migration or Alembic. Keep dependencies minimal: fastapi, uvicorn, sqlalchemy, psycopg[binary], pydantic, bcrypt, pytest, httpx, ruff. No Redis, Celery, background worker, Docker Compose or PDF library. The app must start in under 10 seconds with under 512 MB RAM and cope with free-tier sleep and cold starts. Background work runs only through POST /internal/run-jobs, called every 15 minutes by a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow with the secret JOBS_SECRET. Emails go through one send_email() function: print to the log by default, use a free email API (e.g., Resend) only if EMAIL_API_KEY is set. Charts: a few simple CSS bars or one small Chart.js script from a CDN. All settings come from environment variables (DATABASE_URL, SECRET_KEY, JOBS_SECRET, EMAIL_API_KEY, OWNER_EMAIL, OWNER_PASSWORD for the seed); include .env.example and never commit secrets. Provide a small Dockerfile (python:3.12-slim) so the app runs the same everywhere. CI/CD with GitHub Actions: (1) ci.yml on every pull request and push: ruff lint, pytest against SQLite; (2) deploy.yml on push to main after tests pass: trigger the Render deploy hook (secret RENDER_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL, Render auto-deploy turned off), wait, then smoke test GET /health on the live URL and fail the run if it does not answer; (3) jobs.yml: cron every 15 minutes calling /internal/run-jobs. Write tests for the key rules: no double booking, price snapshot, cancellation deadline, waitlist offer order. Use Europe/Berlin time and EUR everywhere. Seed demo data for Isar Wellness: the menu, two therapists (Lena and Sofia), working hours and about 20 sample bookings. Generate manage and offer tokens with a secure random generator and hash the owner password with bcrypt. Build in thin vertical slices, each merged through a pull request that passes CI and deploys: slice 1 = /health, public menu, owner login and the full pipeline live; slice 2 = availability and booking with items; slice 3 = manage link and emails; slice 4 = owner bookings and receipts; slice 5 = waitlist and run-jobs; slice 6 = dashboard. Keep the core generic (provider, service, booking).
